ecosystem.notes: No filing reports App Store volume, so measure is null and the figure sits in studies[]. The study was paid for by Apple ('Support for this study was provided by Apple'). Its Table 1 total is $1,295B ('nearly $1.3 trillion'). It covers calendar 2024; Apple's fiscal 2024 ended September 28, 2024. About 78% of it ($1,014B) is physical goods and services bought through apps (retail, travel, food delivery, ride hailing), on which Apple takes no commission, and 12% ($150B) is in-app advertising, so it is not App Store sales. The 90% no-commission claim is kept with value null (it is a percentage). The study does not state developer earnings or payouts. platformRevenue is null because Apple's FY2024 10-K does not break out App Store revenue: it is inside Services net sales, and the 10-K says only that 'the Company accounts for all third-party application–related sales on a net basis by recognizing in Services net sales only the commission it retains' and that Services grew 'due primarily to higher net sales from advertising, the App Store® and cloud services' (FY2024 10-K, https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/320193/000032019324000123/aapl-20240928.htm).
